data.name: Midrar
data.gender_notes: Midrar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'd-r-r', which means 'to soften, make gentle, be kind'. In Islamic history, Midrar is a name given to those who are known for their gentle and compassionate nature. The name Midrar carries the meaning “Gentle, Kind” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Midrar usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes kindness, compassion, and gentleness in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Midrar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, Kind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Midrar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: مدرار
in_arabic.meaning: مدرار تعني الشخص الذي يجود بالمال الكثير
in_arabic.long_meaning: مدرار هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني الشخص الذي يجود بالمال الكثير، ويتصف بالكرم والجود. ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر اسم 'مدرار' في سورة ص: وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَرَّ بِهِ مُؤْمِنٌ فَيَقُولُ أَهْلَنِيَ الْمَعْرُوفَ أَوْ أَهْلَنِيَ الْحُسْنَىَ وَهُوَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يَرُدَّهُ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَلَا إِلَى مُؤْمِنٍ أَلا فَإِذَا رَأَى النُّورَ فَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِنهُ وَأَمسَكَ بِالزِّمامِ وَأَصبَحَ مُدرارًا يَقُولُ أَنَا قَد أَخَذتُ مِنهُ وَأَنا أَملِكُهُ وَأَنا أَرُدُّهُ إِذا شِئتُ

in_urdu.name: مدرار
in_urdu.meaning: مدرار کا مطلب ہے بہت زیادہ مال دینے والا شخص
in_urdu.long_meaning: مدرار ایک عربی मूल کا مذکر نام ہے جو بہت زیادہ مال دینے والے شخص کو کہا جاتا ہے۔ یہ نام قرآن مجید میں سورة ص میں ذکر ہوا ہے۔ مدرار کے معنی کثرت دینے کے ہیں، یعنی جو شخص بہت زیادہ دینے کی عادت رکھتا ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے اور اس کا انتخاب اسلامی ثقافت میں رواج رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मिदरार
in_hindi.meaning: मिदरार का अर्थ है बहुत अधिक धन देने वाला व्यक्ति
in_hindi.long_meaning: मिदरार एक अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम है, जिसका अर्थ है बहुत अधिक धन देने वाला व्यक्ति। यह नाम कुरआन में सूरत साद में उल्लेखित है। मिदरार का अर्थ है अधिक देने वाला, यानी जो व्यक्ति बहुत अधिक देने की आदत रखता है। यह नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है और इसका चयन इस्लामी संस्कृति में प्रचलित है।

in_pashto.name: مدرار
in_pashto.meaning: مدرار د ډېرې پيسې ورکړوونکی سړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مدرار د عربي اصلي مذکر نوم دی، چې د ډېرې پيسې ورکړوونکی سړی په معنی دی. دا نوم په قرآن کريم کې د ص سورې په آيتونو کې راغلی دی. مدرار د ډېر ورکړو معنی لري، يعنې هغه څوک چې ډېری پيسې ورکړی. دا نوم په اسلامي کلیو کې مهم ګڼل کیږي او په اسلامي کلتور کې د ده انتخاب رواج دی.

in_english.name: Midrar
in_english.long_meaning: Midrar is a masculine name of Arabic origin, meaning 'one who gives abundantly' or 'generous'. It is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Sad, verse 31. The name Midrar signifies a person known for their generosity and open-handedness. In Islamic tradition, the name is associated with positive attributes such as kindness, charity, and magnanimity. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the values of generosity and benevolence.

historical_references.reference: Al-Mas'udi, Muruj Al-Dhahab wa Ma'adin Al-Jawhar. Book 2, Chapter 11: The History of Yemen, Midrar Ibn Al-Akhtal.
historical_references.context: Midrar Ibn Al-Akhtal was a renowned poet of the Umayyad period in Yemen. He converted to Islam and became a close friend of the Umayyad caliph, Hisham Ibn Abdul-Malik. Midrar is known for his panegyrics and poetic compositions in praise of the caliph and the Islamic faith.

historical_references.reference: Al-Biruni, Al-Athar Al-Biqayah fi Tarekh Al-Hind. Section 16: Description of the Country of Sind, Midrar Ibn Ghiyath Al-Khawarizmi.
historical_references.context: Midrar Ibn Ghiyath Al-Khawarizmi was a Persian scholar, mathematician, and astronomer. He is best known for his contributions to mathematics under the Abbasid Caliphate. He traveled extensively, including to Sind, where he was involved in the translation of Hindu works into Arabic. Midrar's works on mathematics and astronomy significantly influenced the development of these sciences in the Islamic world.
